headline: The Grand Ole Opry's first broadcast
post_facts: Began as the WSM Barn Dance
Still on the air a century later

scenes.text: [warmly] On this day, in nineteen twenty-five... a little radio show began in Nashville.

scenes.label: Ryman Auditorium
scenes.caption: The Opry's home until 1974
scenes.text: [thoughtfully] Announcer George D. Hay called it the WSM Barn Dance.

scenes.label: year-old fiddler played first
scenes.text: [calmly] The first star was Uncle Jimmy Thompson, a seventy-seven-year-old fiddler.

scenes.label: WSM, Nashville
scenes.caption: Opry souvenir album, about 1957
scenes.text: [softly] In nineteen twenty-seven, Hay gave it a new name... the Grand Ole Opry.

scenes.title: Still on the air
scenes.text: [warmly] A century later, it is still on the air.

scenes.title: Ever been to the Opry?
scenes.text: [gently] Have you ever been to the Opry?
